fix_commit.message: Bug 1942169 - Dispatch messages to the current thread r=asuth
fix_commit.author: Olli Pettay

findings.title: Thread-unsafe dispatch in ServiceWorkerContainer
findings.message: The `EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch` function unconditionally uses `NS_DispatchToMainThread` to dispatch messages. However, when ServiceWorkerContainer is exposed on worker threads (via WorkerNavigator), this causes messages to be dispatched to the main thread instead of the worker thread. This results in a race condition where the worker's JS runtime may be accessed from the main thread while it's being used on the worker thread, leading to memory safety violations and potential exploitation.

related_locations.description: DispatchMessage function receives messages from wrong thread, removed MOZ_ASSERT(NS_IsMainThread()) in this commit which should have been a warning sign

findings.suggestion: When exposing ServiceWorkerContainer to worker threads, the dispatch mechanism must dispatch to the current thread (the thread that owns the ServiceWorkerContainer), not unconditionally to the main thread. Use `NS_DispatchToCurrentThread` instead of `NS_DispatchToMainThread`.

ground_truth.root_cause: When exposing ServiceWorkerContainer to worker threads in Bug 1131324, the code change removed `MOZ_ASSERT(NS_IsMainThread())` from `DispatchMessage()` to allow it to work on worker threads, but failed to update the corresponding `EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch()` function. This function still used `NS_DispatchToMainThread`, causing messages to always be dispatched to the main thread regardless of which thread the ServiceWorkerContainer belongs to.

must_cover.reason: Contains the vulnerable code that unconditionally dispatches to the main thread using NS_DispatchToMainThread, regardless of whether the ServiceWorkerContainer belongs to a window (main thread) or worker (worker thread). This causes messages to be dispatched to the wrong thread when the container is on a worker, leading to race conditions where the worker's JS runtime may be accessed from the main thread while in use on the worker thread.

This function was modified in Bug 1131324 to support worker threads (MOZ_ASSERT(NS_IsMainThread()) was removed), but the corresponding caller EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch was not updated. A reviewer must see that DispatchMessage can execute on worker threads but is being dispatched to the main thread unconditionally, creating a thread-safety violation. The function accesses JS context and global objects that must be accessed on the correct thread.

This function receives messages from service workers and calls EnqueueReceivedMessageDispatch. A reviewer must understand that this function can be called on either the main thread (for window contexts) or worker threads (for worker contexts), and the dispatching must respect the current thread context. The function makes no thread checks before calling the vulnerable dispatch function.

This function exposes ServiceWorkerContainer on worker threads via WorkerNavigator.serviceWorker, making it accessible in worker contexts. This is the code path introduced in Bug 1131324 that enabled the vulnerability. A reviewer must understand that ServiceWorkerContainer can now exist on worker threads, not just main thread, which makes the thread-agnostic dispatch critical.

This function delivers messages to ServiceWorkerContainer by calling container->ReceiveMessage(). A reviewer must understand that this call can occur on any thread (main or worker) depending on where the ServiceWorkerContainer lives. The function operates on the thread owning the ClientSource/global object, which can be a worker thread, triggering the race condition when the message is incorrectly dispatched to the main thread.
